Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 2, Verse 6

“We do not even know which is better — that we should conquer them, or that they should conquer us. The very sons of Dhritarashtra, after killing whom we would not wish to live, stand arrayed before us.”

This is Arjuna's deepest confusion: both outcomes look like loss. Winning means living among the dead he loved; losing means the same grief with defeat added. He cannot locate a good result anywhere.
